summary: Fire lookout near Boston Bar, BC: manned from 1957, decommissioned 1993, rebuilt 2012-13, burned in the Kookipi Creek wildfire on 17 August 2023.

facts.design: Tapered wooden lookout tower; the 2012-13 rebuild matched the original's look and dimensions
facts.status_note: Burned in a wildfire on 17 August 2023; the Four Wheel Drive Association of BC planned a rebuild

staffing.status: observers each fire season until the early 1970s; no longer staffed

events.note: Built between 1956 and 1958 per Recreation Sites and Trails BC, as quoted by Global News; the club says late 1950s. 1956 is the earliest year of that range
Officially decommissioned as a fire lookout tower
Collapsed under heavy snow in winter
Rebuilt by the Four Wheel Drive Association and Southwest All Terrain Trails; a Canada Lookouts timeline says work began in August 2012 and was completed in September 2013
Formally established as a BC recreation site
Consumed by the Kookipi Creek wildfire on 17 August 2023; the fire had started from lightning on 8 July

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Our West Coast says the tower was rebuilt in 2012. The Canada Lookouts timeline says rebuilding began in August 2012 and was completed in September 2013. The story reports both.

Recreation Sites and Trails BC gives 1956 to 1958 for the original tower (via Global News). The club says the late 1950s, and Our West Coast says the lookout was manned from 1957. These do not contradict each other.

notes_for_editor: Access is not footnoted. The BC recreation-site record for this site (REC166414, in data/sources/bc_rec_sites.json) reads 'CLOSED DUE TO WILDFIRE DAMAGE - NO ACCESS' and gives an establishment date of 2013-12-05. That record comes from a bulk WFS download, so no cached page carries the quote, and the sitesandtrailsbc.ca resource page would not load in the reader. Check https://www.sitesandtrailsbc.ca/resource/REC166414 before publishing any access statement. The record has no local_unit. The built year is a range (1956-1958), so the event uses 1956, the earliest year. The rebuild completion date conflicts (2012 vs September 2013) and both are stated in the story. The 4WDABC post dates the rebuild '11 years almost to the day' before the fire, which points to about August 2012 and sits oddly with the September 2013 completion; the story gives this as the club's own claim and does not resolve the conflict. Global News calls Matt Ion 'communicators director'; the story says 'communications director'. Wikidata Q131312883 gives the same coordinates and calls it a fire lookout tower; it is not cited.
